chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Usman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who lodges with the man and has a debt upon him, can he eat from his food? He (peace be upon him) said: Yes, he eats from his food for three days, then he should not eat anything after that.
ai.seo_question: How long can a debtor eat at a creditor's house without paying?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the customary hospitality rights of a debtor staying with a creditor, limiting the free consumption of food to three days. This ruling reflects the pre-Islamic and early Islamic social norm where hosting a guest, even for debt, was a moral obligation, but after three days, the guest becomes a burden unless they contribute or receive explicit permission. It highlights the balance between maintaining social ties (silat al-rahim) and preventing financial exploitation in personal relationships.
